ACCEPTUnder the unchanged pairwise endpoint-disjoint canonical-source model, and with the complete ambient configuration satisfying the established ledger’s hypotheses as you state them, the corollary follows. The signs, the identification with  $\Phi(Y)$ , and the restricted scope are correct.For a standalone statement, I would explicitly retain pairwise endpoint-disjointness, the common tile phase, and containment of every retained support in the ambient rectangle. These are inherited from your stated model; they do not require a new compensation theorem.1. The ledger substitution is exactTaking the complete-fusion ledger in your question as established,
$$\sigma:=\frac{mn}{2}-|T|-|M|
\ge N_{\mathrm{pos}}+S+C-K_{\mathrm{irr}}-G.$$
Every original in the entire family has charge either  $-1$  or  $1-h$ . Since  $h\ge6$ , all charges are strictly negative. Therefore
$$N_{\mathrm{pos}}=0,\qquad
S=a+(h-1)b.$$
There are no positive-charge U originals on which a positive-U side can be marked, so  $G=0$ .Now substitute the established identities
$$C=2J-K_{\mathrm{reg}},
\qquad
K=K_{\mathrm{reg}}+K_{\mathrm{irr}}.$$
This gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\sigma
&\ge S+2J-K_{\mathrm{reg}}-K_{\mathrm{irr}}\\
&=S+2J-K\\
&=\Phi(Y).
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is valid because, as stipulated,  $J$  is exactly the mixed-full-tile count and  $K$  is exactly the count of original directed, source-labelled events used in the audited inventory. The original supports remain immutable for that event definition, including when another original endpoint consumes them.No separate nonnegativity assumption on  $C$ , or separate estimate on either event subclass, is needed. Their exact combination is what matters.The audited common-height theorem then yields
$$\Phi(Y)\ge a+\left(\frac h2-1\right)b,$$
and hence
$$\boxed{
|T|+|M|
\le
\frac{mn}{2}
-a-\left(\frac h2-1\right)b.
}$$
Equivalently,
$$|T|
\le
\frac{mn}{2}
-|M|
-a-\left(\frac h2-1\right)b.$$
Thus the coefficient of  $|M|$  is indeed  $1$  on this complete class, with the stated additional slack. Since  $h\ge6$ , that slack is at least  $a+2b$ , and therefore at least the number  $a+b$  of originals.2. Hypotheses that should remain explicitPairwise endpoint-disjointness. This is essential to both the audited transverse-family theorem and the canonical complete-fusion application. Your reference to the originals “just audited” imports it, but the standalone corollary should say it explicitly. Merely requiring that  $P$  and  $M$  are unions, with no subsequent modification, would not by itself assert disjointness of the original endpoint sets.The same aligned physical tiles throughout. The common strip must retain its audited phase, and the ambient rectangle must be aligned with that same partition. An even translation in both coordinates preserves bar parity and all physical tiles. With even side lengths and an aligned corner, the ambient rectangle is a union of whole tiles, so no original receiver tile is truncated at its boundary.Full support retention and ambient containment. There must be no boundary convention that silently discards an original support. Your hypotheses already supply this on their natural reading. Indeed, writing  $H_{\mathrm{all}}$  for the union of original supports and  $R$  for the ambient rectangle,
$$P\subseteq R,
\qquad
H_{\mathrm{all}}\setminus P\subseteq R$$
imply  $H_{\mathrm{all}}\subseteq R$ : consumed supports lie in  $P$ , and every other support remains occupied inside  $R$ . Thus no additional padding hypothesis is needed, but an endpoint-only interpretation of “the originals lie inside” must not be used to permit clipped supports.The ledger’s meaning of  $T$ . Keep  $T$  as the object denoted by  $T$  in the established complete-fusion ledger. The original endpoint union is  $P$ , as you have specified. There is no step here replacing  $|T|$  by  $|P|$ .The conditions on optional selections are also correctly retained. They must satisfy the established ledger’s restrictions and belong to the same feasible final configuration. In particular, selections outside every original receiver tile cannot introduce an unaccounted filling of a tile containing original endpoints. No endpoint creation or matching modification changes the original inventory being used.With these inherited conventions explicit, I find no additional substantive hypothesis missing.3. The stated scope is correctThe whole-family premise is decisive: every original source entering the ambient ledger belongs to the audited common-height transverse class. This lets the complete ambient ledger’s entire source contribution, mixed-tile count, and event count be identified with the same  $\Phi(Y)$ .A transverse-only pocket inside a larger seed containing other orientations does not satisfy that premise. Your explicit exclusion of that application is therefore correct, and the corollary assigns no sign to an uncontrolled exterior contribution.The sharp endpoint-only odd-pair examples establish sharpness of a coefficient in the earlier inventory inequality. They do not establish equality in this ambient corollary. Ambient equality would require, at minimum, both
$$\sigma=\Phi(Y)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Phi(Y)=a+\left(\frac h2-1\right)b,$$
together with an admissible complete ambient realization. None of that follows merely from endpoint-only sharpness, and you make no such claim.Accordingly, this is a valid restricted complete-class improvement, with extra slack. The horizontal-U/rotor cases, mixed-orientation seeds, exterior sign, and unrestricted global objectives remain open. The deduction requires no finite verification and makes no new end-to-end Lean claim.
